title: Xanthe and the Clock
premise: In the port city of Vellamare, on the eve of the printers' revolution, Wren Ashgrove works in her late father's print shop, cutting type and hiding the fact that she has been secretly printing seditious broadsheets under his name. When a census taker named Xanthe arrives asking one question too many about who really runs the press, Wren realizes the state is closing a net around the city's dissidents — and that her father's death was no accident. Together with Xanthe, whose loyalty to the regime fractures as they uncover the records of confiscated estates, Wren races to set the true account of the crackdown in type and smuggle it aboard the last neutral ship before the victors can burn the shop and rewrite history. The book ends at dawn: the ship sails carrying the printed truth, Wren stays behind to face the new order with nothing but her name finally on the record.
about_author: Lena Nakamura is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about people whose work leaves marks the world tries to erase.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She measures the print shop by what can be carried — type cases, the hand press, her father's cutting tools — while rumors of the coming orders spread through the harbor district. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: One Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A census taker with meticulous habits interviews Wren about household composition and presses the question of who operates the press since her father died. Wren lies; Xanthe notices. Emotional beat: two careful people circling each other.

chapters.title: The Dead Man's Matrix
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sorting her father's effects, she finds a hidden matrix stamped with a seal she doesn't recognize — proof he was printing for someone powerful. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Ledgers of the Confiscated
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Filing census returns at the registry, Xanthe glimpses seizure ledgers listing Ashgrove among estates taken before the owner's 'accidental' death. Emotional beat: first crack in institutional faith.

chapters.title: Broadsheet at Midnight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren prints another seditious broadsheet under her father's name, nearly caught by a patrol. Her neighbor Odile, a fishwife, covers for her. Emotional beat: fear braided with defiance.

chapters.title: The Second Visit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe returns with follow-up questions that are clearly not census questions, probing the shop's output and clients. Wren deflects; both know it's a game now. Emotional beat: mutual recognition of adversaries who might be allies.

chapters.title: What the Harbor Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tells Wren how the customs men changed after the Ashgrove seizure, and which clerk signed the papers. Emotional beat: the neighborhood's collective memory as an archive.

chapters.title: The Registry Fire
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A fire destroys part of the records office — conveniently, the seizure ledgers. Xanthe had copied a page out of habit. Emotional beat: horror at realizing erasure is policy.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A government printer offers Wren a contract to print victory proclamations — a bribe and a leash. She accepts to buy time and access. Emotional beat: self-disgust as strategy.

chapters.title: The Copied Page
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Unable to file the copied ledger page through channels, Xanthe brings it to the one person it names: Wren. Emotional beat: the moment adversaries become conspirators.

chapters.title: Terms of Trust
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Xanthe negotiate an uneasy alliance: truth on the record, but whose record? They inventory what evidence survives. Emotional beat: fragile, transactional trust.

chapters.title: The Compositor's Oath
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile gathers the harbor's witnesses — dockers, a defrocked priest, a customs deserter — each holding a fragment of the story. Emotional beat: found family assembling around a table.

chapters.title: Setting the First Line
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren begins composing the true account in type, hidden inside a legitimate job. Each word chosen like a stone. Emotional beat: craft as resistance.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Dinner
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe is summoned to dine with Inspector Corvane, architect of the confiscations, who praises their thoroughness and hints they are being watched. Emotional beat: terror dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: A Name on the Door
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers her father's real client list — including Corvane himself, before the seizures began. Betrayal upon betrayal. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under grief.

chapters.title: The Deserter's Testimony
chapters.summary: The deserter Bram's POV. Bram recounts the night of the Ashgrove raid from the soldiers' side, confirming murder on orders. Emotional beat: guilt seeking absolution through witness.

chapters.title: Paper Chase
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe traces the surviving duplicate ledgers to a monastery archive outside the walls, planning retrieval. Emotional beat: methodical hope.

chapters.title: The Monastery Copy
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Xanthe travel together, posing as pilgrims, and copy the ledgers by lamplight. First unguarded conversation between them. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared risk.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Back home, the crackdown begins: arrests at dawn, the harbor sealed, ships restricted. Odile hides Bram in her cellar. Emotional beat: the noose tightening on everyone at once.

chapters.title: Return to a Changed City
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Xanthe slip back through checkpoints to find neighbors gone and the shop watched. Emotional beat: home rendered foreign overnight.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe identifies the leak in their circle — young Teo, the apprentice, coerced by threats to his mother. Mercy versus security. Emotional beat: compassion as a costly choice.

chapters.title: Teo's Choice
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Confronted gently rather than punished, Teo confesses everything and offers to feed false information back to Corvane. Emotional beat: shame transformed into agency.

chapters.title: False Plates
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The circle feeds Corvane a decoy plan while the real text goes to press in sections disguised as hymnals. Emotional beat: exhilaration of the con.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes In
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The inspector, suspicious, orders the shop raided for the morning after next — and requisitions the only ship due to sail on the tide. Emotional beat: cold, patient menace.

chapters.title: The Hymnal Trick
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe audits the disguised pages and finds three signatures missing — testimony that must be sworn before sailing. Emotional beat: perfectionism against the clock.

chapters.title: Sworn in a Cellar
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. By candlelight in Odile's cellar, the witnesses sign and swear their accounts. Odile feeds them all first. Emotional beat: a family made of oaths.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Soldiers storm the shop early; Wren springs her father's old trap — a false wall behind the type racks — but the press itself cannot be saved. Emotional beat: sacrifice of the thing she loves most.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Carried
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Watching the press dismantled, Wren grieves her father properly for the first time, understanding the shop was never the inheritance — the truth was. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Turned Clerk
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Xanthe burns their own career down, filing a formal protest that puts their name beside Wren's on the record. Emotional beat: liberation in ruin.

chapters.title: Harbor of Locked Gates
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the ship requisitioned, Odile leverages every favor in the fish market to reach the harbormaster's corrupt deputy. Emotional beat: the poor's economy of favors.

chapters.title: The Bribe and the Blade
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. Teo delivers the deputy's payment but is followed; he leads the tail away from the others, straight into a patrol. Emotional beat: courage without guarantee.

chapters.title: Cost of Passage
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. News of Teo's arrest; the circle debates fleeing without him. Wren refuses to leave anyone off the record or off the ship. Emotional beat: the theme of justice outside the law made personal.

chapters.title: Cell Visit
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Using their last official credential, Xanthe visits Teo and arranges his transfer — into their own custody, then out of it. Emotional beat: the system turned against itself.

chapters.title: Night Move
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The whole circle moves the printed sheets through the drainage tunnels to the quay, Bram navigating routes he once patrolled. Emotional beat: tense, breath-held momentum.

chapters.title: Boarding at Black Tide
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Loading the crates past a bribed mate and a watchful naval officer, Wren faces Corvane on the quay — recognition, threat, and a bluff that holds. Emotional beat: the climax's held breath.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The ship clears the harbor as Corvane's warrant arrives minutes too late. Xanthe watches Vellamare shrink, choosing exile over safety. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: What the Ship Carries
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At sea, the circle reads the finished account aloud — every name, every signature, Teo's included. Emotional beat: mourning and celebration in one voice.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historians
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. In the burned registry, Corvane commissions the official history and finds, already circulating abroad, a version he cannot suppress. Emotional beat: the futility of erasure.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Years later, in a foreign print shop, Wren sets her own name in type for the first edition bearing it — author, witness, daughter. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Clock Keeps Time
chapters.summary: Ensemble coda. On the anniversary, letters arrive in Vellamare from readers of the smuggled book; Odile reads them aloud where the shop stood. The clock above the ruined doorway still runs. Emotional beat: enduring, communal hope.
